prior_block:
PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 7 "Service technician hours": indemnified in all 3 earlier cases; when indemnified t per hr about 84 (80% range 56 to 106); revealed per hr: 44-49 (case 21), >=81 (case 39), >=81 (case 39), so this line (6.75 hr) about 566 (381 to 715)
- line 8 "Helper hours": no earlier line of this grade; level of the other hourly grades; when indemnified t per hr about 68 (80% range 27 to 173), so this line (5.75 hr) about 394 (156 to 992)
- line 9 "Rock wool pipe insulation": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 24 (80% range 17.9 to 37); revealed per pc: >=22 (case 39), so this line (6 pc) about 146 (107 to 222)
- line 12 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 13 of 28 earlier cases, t = 0 in 15; when indemnified t per pc about 80 (80% range 72 to 88); revealed per pc: >=76 (case 21), >=76 (case 21), >=74 (case 27), >=83 (case 34), >=76 (case 34), >=65 (case 39)
- line 13 "Construction waste disposal": indemnified in the one earlier case; when indemnified t per pc about 62 (80% range 45 to 94); revealed per pc: >=57 (case 18)
- line 17 "Processing flat fee": NOT indemnified (t = 0) in all 6 earlier cases; no price evidence

items.rationale: The indoor heating-pipe repair is covered under 2.4.3(a), and matching fittings are covered under 7.1.7(c). Four elbows at about €10 gross each give €40.

Under 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e), these fittings are payable only if the repair involved a documented 28 mm connection; the only replacement tube listed is 15 mm. If verified, five elbows at about €19 each give €95.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) require this fitting to match the actual repair. No 28 mm connection is documented; if verified, one elbow is estimated at €19 gross.
Minor fasteners used in the pipe repair are covered under 7.1.7(c) and need not be individually traced under 7.1.8(e). Eight at about €1.50 each give €12.

Necessary supports for the repaired run are covered under 7.1.7(c), but 7.1.8(e) excludes clamps that do not fit the documented installation. The 25 mm size is not explained by the 15 mm tube alone; if verified, four at €5 each give €20.
Like-for-like copper tubing for the failed indoor heating run is covered under 2.4.3(a) and 7.1.7(c). At about €13 gross per metre, 6.4 m comes to €83.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers customary labour for the pipe repair, not labour on the unrelated jobs. The supplied gross benchmark for 6.75 hours is €566 if those hours are attributable to the repair.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary helper time attributable to the repair; the straightforward scope makes the full allocation less certain. The supplied gross benchmark for 5.75 hours is €394.
Restoring the existing rock wool insulation is covered under 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9. The supplied benchmark for all six pieces is €146 gross.

Wire used to secure the replacement insulation qualifies under 7.1.7(c), but 7.1.8(e) excludes excess stock not attributable to the repair. If the 2 kg charge is substantiated, about €8 per kg gives €16.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.8(e) allow a lump sum for installation consumables actually used, excluding duplicate charges under 7.1.8(c). A modest gross allowance is €18.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel charge per contractor per invoice, and this is the only one. The supplied gross benchmark is €80.

Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover disposal of the removed pipe and insulation, not waste from the undamaged storage-room floor. The €62 benchmark applies if the charge is attributable to covered repair debris.
Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude repainting the unaffected hallway; it is not part of a continuous affected surface under 7.1.6. The conditional estimate is 12 m² at €15 gross per m².
Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude replacement of the laminate in the separate, undamaged storage room. The conditional estimate is 15 m² at €55 gross per m².
Section 7.1.8(a) excludes routine servicing unrelated to the insured heating-pipe failure. The conditional estimate for the service is €85 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes processing charges added to itemised labour and materials. The conditional gross estimate is €15.
